title: Protocol for Decoding the Protein Composition of Whole Nucleosomes with Nuc-MS: Sample Preparation, Data Acquisition and Analysis
protocol: Resuspend cell pellet with 2.5X PCV of Buffer A (composition as provided).
Add equal volume of Buffer A supplemented with 2% Triton X-100 to lyse cells.
Incubate on ice for 10 mins with occasional mixing.
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,300 xg for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend nuclei pellet with 6X PCV of Buffer A.
Transfer nuclei suspension onto a sucrose cushion (composition as provided).
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,300 xg for 12 minutes at 4°C to separate from debris.
Resuspend nuclei pellet with 2X PCV of Buffer A.
Incubate the resuspended nuclei at room temperature for 5 mins.
Supplement nuclei suspension with 1 mM CaCl2.
Add 2 µL of NEB micrococcal nuclease per 1 mL of cell suspension to the nuclei suspension.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes with occasional mixing.
To quench micrococcal nuclease digestion, incubate on ice and supplement nuclei suspension with 2 mM EGTA and 1 mM EDTA.
Supplement nuclei suspension with final concentration of 100 mM KCl and 0.05% Triton X-100.
Incubate 15 minutes on ice with occasional mixing.
Centrifuge at 20,000 xg for 20 minutes at 4°C and collect resulting supernatant containing nucleosomes.
Concentrate and buffer exchange mononucleosomes into Buffer A supplemented with 650 mM NaCl using a 30 kDa MWCO spin filter.
Purify concentrated nucleosomes using HiPrep™ 26/60 Sephacryl S-300 HR column equilibrated with Buffer A supplemented with 650 mM NaCl.
Validate fractions containing mononucleosomes by purifying 10 ug of material using Qiagen DNA cleanup kit and resolving it on a 2% agarose gel in 0.5X TBE.
Concentrate purified mononucleosomes and synthetic nucleosomes into 150 mM ammonium acetate solution using the 0.5 mL 30 kDa MWCO spin filter.
Condition the filter by spinning 500 µL of 150 mM ammonium acetate for 3 minutes at 13,000 xg.
Add up to 500 µL of Nuc sample into the filter – topping off with ammonium acetate – and spin for 5 mins at 13,000 xg or until sample is concentrated at or below 100 µL.
For sample desalting, add ammonium acetate up to the 500 µL mark and spin sample for 5 mins at 13,000 xg.
Repeat desalting process 10-15 times for best results.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes to concentrate sample >2 µM in <50 µL.
Set injection time to 50 ms for QE-EMR and 200 ms for QE-UHMR.
Set number of microscans to 10 for both instruments.
Adjust resolution (MS1) to 15,000 at 400 m/z for QE-EMR and 17,500 at 200 m/z for QE-UHMR.
Maintain Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Pressure at 4 V: 1.65E-9 mBar and 2-4 V: 7.7E-11 to 1.55E-10 mBar.
Apply Source Induced Dissociation (SID) of 25 V for QE-EMR and 5 V for QE-UHMR.
Enable In-Source Trapping (IST) at 25 to 50 V for QE-UHMR.
Set HCD trapping energy to 10 V for QE-EMR and 0 V for QE-UHMR.
Adjust capillary temperature to 330 ºC for QE-EMR and 300 ºC for QE-UHMR.
Set injection time to 1000-2000 ms for MS^3 and pseudo-MS^3 fragmentation.
Isolate the desired histone proteoform charge state using a quadrupole mass filter with an isolation window of 5-10 m/z.
Collect 10 microscans per sample during data acquisition.
Set resolution to 120,000 at 400 m/z for MS^2 analysis on QE-EMR and 100,000 at 200 m/z on QE-UHMR.
Maintain ultra-high vacuum pressure at 7.11E-10 mBar for QE-EMR and 7.7E-11 mBar for QE-UHMR.
Apply source induced dissociation (SID) of 50 V for QE-EMR; do not apply SID for QE-UHMR.
Use in-source trapping (IST) at 150 to 200 V exclusively on the QE-UHMR.
Set HCD trapping energy to 120 V for QE-EMR and 30-40 V (Normalized Collision Energy, NCE) for QE-UHMR.
